sections.title: Oral defenses: 10 deep ladders x 8 follow-ups

keyTerms.definition: Define -> toy -> derive -> implement -> compare -> debug -> critique -> design.
Oral format. Keys in keys-oral.

recall.question: How does each oral ladder run?
recall.answer: Define, toy, derive, implement/complexity, compare, debug, critique, design.

sections.title: O1. From the attention bottleneck to FlashAttention

keyTerms.definition: Materializing the T x T score matrix: O(T^2) memory and traffic.
Running max and normalizer per block; O(T d) memory, never the T^2 matrix.
Wins when sharp selection decides quality: copy, retrieval.

recall.question: O1a. Define the attention bottleneck in one sentence.
recall.answer: Attention materializes a T x T score matrix: O(T^2) memory and traffic dominate.

recall.question: O1b. T=8192, d=128, one head. Compute score FLOPs and score memory.
recall.answer: 17.2 TFLOPs scores, 256 MiB fp32 per head.

recall.question: O1f. Your tiled attention is 2x slower than naive at T=512. Why?
recall.answer: Tiling overhead dominates at small T: the naive kernel fits in SRAM anyway.

sections.title: O2. From scaling laws to the emergence audit

keyTerms.definition: Loss as a power law of scale: straight line in log-log space.
-0.0748 per decade on the toy fit.
A step metric on a smooth skill ramp; the jump is in the measurement.

recall.question: O2a. Define a scaling law.
recall.answer: Loss as a power law of scale: straight line in log-log space.

recall.question: O2b. Fit the two-point law and predict the third scale.
O2h. Design the emergence audit for a vendor’s “emergent ability” claim.
recall.answer: Demand continuous scores. Replot vs scale. The jump should flatten to a ramp.

keyTerms.definition: The batch re-forms every decode iteration.
The 0.5 s gap: waiting, not speed.
Splits big prefills so decodes stop stalling.

recall.question: O3a. Define iteration-level scheduling.
recall.answer: The batch re-forms every decode iteration.

recall.question: O3b. Compute continuous vs static mean latency on the 4-request trace.
recall.answer: 1.0 s vs 1.5 s mean latency.

recall.question: O3h. Capacity plan: how many GPUs for a bursty trace at a p99 SLO?
recall.answer: Simulate the trace: find GPUs where p99 <= SLO with bounded admission. Add headroom for the burst factor.

keyTerms.definition: Score experts, keep top-k, renormalize, weight the outputs.
(tokens*k/experts)*factor; overflow tokens drop.
Fixes skew; over-weighted kills specialization, under-weighted collapses.

recall.question: O4a. Define top-k expert routing.
recall.answer: Score experts, keep top-k, renormalize, weight the outputs.

recall.question: O4c. Derive the capacity formula and the drop count when expert 0 gets 40 tokens.
recall.answer: Capacity = 64*2/8*1.25 = 20. Expert 0 drops 20 of 40.

recall.question: O4h. Design the production MoE: pick k, factor, and the drop policy for a latency SLO.
recall.answer: k=2, factor ~1.25, drop-with-residual for throughput (or no-drop for quality). Verify against the p99 SLO.

keyTerms.definition: Recurrence (streaming), convolution view (parallel), scan (tree).
Kernel taps K_k = C A^k B.
What the scan combine needs; failure breaks the tree.

recall.question: O5a. Define the three views.
recall.answer: Recurrence (streaming), convolution view (parallel), scan (tree).

recall.question: O5b. Run the recurrence, unroll the kernel, combine the tree. Give the numbers.
O5g. Critique the FFT conv-view “always wins” claim.
recall.answer: Per-call kernel materialization dominates: 127 ms FFT vs 67 ms loop at T=16384. Materialize once, or pay per call.

keyTerms.definition: Idle stage time: (p-1)/(m+p-1).
Same bubble with less activation memory.
Uneven stages break the equal-stages assumption.

recall.question: O6a. Define stages, microbatches, bubble.
recall.answer: Stages: layer groups. Microbatches: batch splits. Bubble: idle stage time.

recall.question: O6b. p=4, m=8. Compute the bubble.
O6h. Design a pipeline for 8 uneven stages: how do you split and verify?
recall.answer: Profile per-layer cost, balance stages by time not layer count, verify with measured idle vs the formula.

keyTerms.definition: 1: optimizer states. 2: +gradients. 3: +params.
fp16 params 2B + fp16 grads 2B + fp32 master 4B + m 4B + v 4B.
Stage 3 adds per-layer param all-gather.

recall.question: O7a. Define the three ZeRO stages.
recall.answer: ZeRO-1: optimizer states. -2: +gradients. -3: +params.

recall.question: O7b. 10B params, 8 GPUs. Compute ZeRO-3 vs DP bytes per GPU.
recall.answer: ZeRO-3: 20.0 GB/GPU. DP: 160 GB/GPU.

recall.question: O7h. Design the memory plan for a 70B run on your cluster.
recall.answer: ZeRO-3/FSDP: 14*70e9/n per GPU. Pick n so per-GPU < 80% of HBM. Keep TP intra-node.

keyTerms.definition: s = (max-min)/(2^b-1), z = round(-min/s).
Each row its own ruler; 218x on the quiet channel.
3-seed eval: task delta >= -0.5%, latency win confirmed.

recall.question: O8a. Define s, z, and the quantization map.
recall.answer: s = (max-min)/(2^b-1), z = round(-min/s). x_q = clamp(round(x/s)+z).

recall.question: O8b. Quantize 0.5 with min=-1, max=1, 4 bits.
O8h. Design the ship/no-ship experiment for int8 serving.
recall.answer: 3-seed eval: task delta >= -0.5%, latency win confirmed, then ship.

keyTerms.definition: ANN -> filter -> cross-encoder rerank.
The reranker: 400/405 of the cascade cost.
ANN recall 0.95: 1 in 20 golds never reach the reranker.

recall.question: O9a. Define the cascade stages.
recall.answer: ANN -> filter -> cross-encoder rerank.

recall.question: O9b. Compute the cascade cost (ANN + 20x20 ms rerank).
O9h. Design the RAG serving stack under a 4 s SLO.
recall.answer: Funnel 100->20->5, quality gate -0.5%, p99 budget with chunked prefills, rollback to keyword search on red.

keyTerms.definition: Per-GPU MTBF / n.
A rack event takes 32 GPUs at once.

recall.question: O10a. Define cluster MTBF.
recall.answer: Mean time between failures for the fleet: per-GPU MTBF / n.

recall.question: O10b. 256 GPUs, 3-year per-GPU MTBF. Compute.
O10h. Design the resilience plan for a 4096-GPU month-long run.
recall.answer: Frequent sharded checkpoints, elastic restart, correlated-failure drills, on-call rotation.
